1.name: Shukla Pratipada
1.title: Day 1 of the waxing moon
1.meaning: The first light after the new moon. Tradition links it to Agni, the sacred fire, and counts it among the joyful (Nanda) days.

2.name: Shukla Dwitiya
2.title: Day 2 of the waxing moon
2.meaning: A thin crescent returns. Linked to Brahma the creator; tradition sees a steady (Bhadra) day for laying foundations.

3.name: Shukla Tritiya
3.title: Day 3 of the waxing moon
3.meaning: Linked to the goddess Gauri. One of the victorious (Jaya) days, traditionally good for beginning things with confidence.

4.name: Shukla Chaturthi
4.title: Day 4 of the waxing moon
4.meaning: Linked to Ganesha, remover of obstacles. An empty (Rikta) day, traditionally used for clearing and finishing rather than starting.

5.name: Shukla Panchami
5.title: Day 5 of the waxing moon
5.meaning: Linked to the serpent deities and to learning. A full (Purna) day, traditionally favourable for study and creative work.

6.name: Shukla Shashthi
6.title: Day 6 of the waxing moon
6.meaning: Linked to Skanda, the young warrior god. A joyful day, traditionally good for courage and steady effort.

7.name: Shukla Saptami
7.title: Day 7 of the waxing moon
7.meaning: Linked to Surya, the Sun. A steady day, traditionally good for travel and for honouring light and warmth.

8.name: Shukla Ashtami
8.title: Day 8 of the waxing moon
8.meaning: The waxing half-moon, linked to the goddess Durga. A victorious day, often kept for devotion and inner strength.

9.name: Shukla Navami
9.title: Day 9 of the waxing moon
9.meaning: Also linked to Durga. An empty day, traditionally used to finish and release rather than to begin.

10.name: Shukla Dashami
10.title: Day 10 of the waxing moon
10.meaning: Linked to Dharma, the right order of things. A full day, traditionally good for decisions and setting direction.

11.name: Shukla Ekadashi
11.title: Day 11 of the waxing moon
11.meaning: Linked to Vishnu. Traditionally a day of fasting or eating lightly, with time set aside for quiet and prayer.

12.name: Shukla Dwadashi
12.title: Day 12 of the waxing moon
12.meaning: Linked to Vishnu. Traditionally the day to gently break the Ekadashi fast and to give to others.

13.name: Shukla Trayodashi
13.title: Day 13 of the waxing moon
13.meaning: Linked to Kama, god of love, and to Shiva at dusk (Pradosha). A victorious day for warmth and connection.

14.name: Shukla Chaturdashi
14.title: Day 14 of the waxing moon
14.meaning: Linked to Shiva. The day before the full moon, an empty day traditionally used for preparation.

15.name: Purnima
15.title: Full moon
15.meaning: The Moon is full and the month peaks. Traditionally a day of celebration, gratitude and rest.

16.name: Krishna Pratipada
16.title: Day 1 of the waning moon
16.meaning: The light begins to recede after the full moon. Traditionally a day to slow down and take stock.

17.name: Krishna Dwitiya
17.title: Day 2 of the waning moon
17.meaning: A steady day as the moon wanes. Tradition favours practical, unhurried work.

18.name: Krishna Tritiya
18.title: Day 3 of the waning moon
18.meaning: A victorious day in the waning half, traditionally good for completing what has been started.

19.name: Krishna Chaturthi
19.title: Day 4 of the waning moon
19.meaning: Linked to Ganesha (Sankashti Chaturthi); many keep a vow until moonrise. An empty day for clearing obstacles.

20.name: Krishna Panchami
20.title: Day 5 of the waning moon
20.meaning: A full day in the waning half. Traditionally good for study, reading and steady routines.

21.name: Krishna Shashthi
21.title: Day 6 of the waning moon
21.meaning: A joyful day as the moon wanes, traditionally used for modest, patient effort.

22.name: Krishna Saptami
22.title: Day 7 of the waning moon
22.meaning: Linked to the Sun. A steady day, traditionally good for order and routine.

23.name: Krishna Ashtami
23.title: Day 8 of the waning moon
23.meaning: The waning half-moon, linked to Durga and Kali. Traditionally a day for devotion and inner strength.

24.name: Krishna Navami
24.title: Day 9 of the waning moon
24.meaning: An empty day, traditionally used for letting go and finishing old tasks.

25.name: Krishna Dashami
25.title: Day 10 of the waning moon
25.meaning: A full day, traditionally good for simple decisions and for preparing for Ekadashi.

26.name: Krishna Ekadashi
26.title: Day 11 of the waning moon
26.meaning: The month's second Ekadashi, linked to Vishnu. Traditionally kept by fasting or eating lightly, and by quiet reflection.

27.name: Krishna Dwadashi
27.title: Day 12 of the waning moon
27.meaning: Traditionally the day to break the Ekadashi fast and to share food with others.

28.name: Krishna Trayodashi
28.title: Day 13 of the waning moon
28.meaning: Linked to Shiva at dusk (Pradosha). Traditionally a quiet evening for prayer or reflection.

29.name: Krishna Chaturdashi
29.title: Day 14 of the waning moon
29.meaning: Linked to Shiva; its night is Masik Shivaratri, a monthly vigil. An empty day before the new moon.

30.name: Amavasya
30.title: New moon
30.meaning: The Moon is dark and the month closes. Traditionally a day to remember ancestors, rest and turn inward.

1.name: Ashwini
1.title: Swift beginnings
1.meaning: The star of the twin horsemen, physicians of the gods. Tradition sees quick, light energy — good for starting and travelling.

2.name: Bharani
2.title: Bearing and restraint
2.meaning: Ruled by Yama, keeper of limits. Tradition sees a day for carrying responsibilities and for discipline rather than ease.

3.name: Krittika
3.title: The cutting flame
3.meaning: Ruled by Agni, the fire. Tradition sees a sharp, purifying energy, good for decisions and cutting away the unnecessary.

4.name: Rohini
4.title: Growth and beauty
4.meaning: Ruled by Brahma and loved by the Moon. A fixed, fertile star, traditionally good for planting, building and lasting work.

5.name: Mrigashira
5.title: The searching deer
5.meaning: Ruled by Soma, the Moon. A gentle, curious energy, traditionally good for exploring, learning and conversation.

6.name: Ardra
6.title: Storm and renewal
6.meaning: Ruled by Rudra, the storm. Tradition sees intensity that clears the air — a day for honest effort, not new ventures.

7.name: Punarvasu
7.title: The return of light
7.meaning: Ruled by Aditi, mother of the gods. A moving, hopeful star, traditionally good for coming home, repairing and starting over.

8.name: Pushya
8.title: Nourishment
8.meaning: Ruled by Brihaspati, teacher of the gods. One of the most favourable stars in tradition, good for learning and care.

9.name: Ashlesha
9.title: The coiled serpent
9.meaning: Ruled by the serpent deities. A sharp, penetrating energy, traditionally linked with insight and with avoiding entanglements.

10.name: Magha
10.title: The throne of ancestors
10.meaning: Ruled by the ancestors (Pitris). Tradition sees a day for honouring lineage and the people who came before.

11.name: Purva Phalguni
11.title: Rest and enjoyment
11.meaning: Ruled by Bhaga, god of delight. Tradition sees a relaxed energy, good for leisure, friendship and creativity.

12.name: Uttara Phalguni
12.title: Partnership and commitment
12.meaning: Ruled by Aryaman, god of agreements. A fixed star, traditionally good for lasting agreements and strengthening relationships.

13.name: Hasta
13.title: The skilled hand
13.meaning: Ruled by Savitar, the Sun's creative power. A light, quick energy, traditionally good for crafts and practical work.

14.name: Chitra
14.title: The bright jewel
14.meaning: Ruled by Tvashtar, the celestial craftsman. A soft star, traditionally good for design, art and making things beautiful.

15.name: Swati
15.title: The independent breeze
15.meaning: Ruled by Vayu, the wind. A moving star, traditionally good for trade, travel and independent action.

16.name: Vishakha
16.title: Focused purpose
16.meaning: Ruled by Indra and Agni together. Tradition sees determination and a goal in sight, with patience needed to reach it.

17.name: Anuradha
17.title: Friendship and devotion
17.meaning: Ruled by Mitra, god of friendship. A soft star, traditionally good for cooperation, groups and loyalty.

18.name: Jyeshtha
18.title: The eldest
18.meaning: Ruled by Indra, king of the gods. Tradition sees responsibility and seniority — a day for leading carefully.

19.name: Mula
19.title: The root
19.meaning: Ruled by Nirriti, goddess of dissolution. Tradition sees a day for getting to the root of things and letting go.

20.name: Purva Ashadha
20.title: Early victory
20.meaning: Ruled by the Waters (Apas). Tradition sees conviction and fresh energy, good for persuading and renewing.

21.name: Uttara Ashadha
21.title: Lasting victory
21.meaning: Ruled by the universal gods (Vishvadevas). A fixed star, traditionally good for steady, principled achievement.

22.name: Shravana
22.title: Listening
22.meaning: Ruled by Vishnu. A moving star, traditionally good for learning, listening and travel.

23.name: Dhanishtha
23.title: Rhythm and abundance
23.meaning: Ruled by the eight Vasus. Tradition sees music, generosity and good timing.

24.name: Shatabhisha
24.title: The hundred physicians
24.meaning: Ruled by Varuna, lord of the cosmic waters. Tradition sees a quiet, inward star linked with secrets and solitude.

25.name: Purva Bhadrapada
25.title: The fierce fire
25.meaning: Ruled by Aja Ekapada, the one-footed goat. Tradition sees intensity and transformation — a day for serious effort.

26.name: Uttara Bhadrapada
26.title: The calm depths
26.meaning: Ruled by Ahir Budhnya, serpent of the deep. A fixed star, traditionally linked with wisdom, patience and steadiness.

27.name: Revati
27.title: Safe journeys
27.meaning: Ruled by Pushan, protector of travellers. The last star, soft and gentle, traditionally good for journeys and completions.

1.name: Vishkambha
1.title: The supporting pillar
1.meaning: Tradition treats it as a yoga of obstacles; new beginnings are usually postponed.

2.name: Priti
2.title: Affection
2.meaning: A favourable yoga, traditionally good for friendship, reconciliation and pleasant meetings.

3.name: Ayushman
3.title: Long life
3.meaning: A favourable yoga, traditionally good for undertakings meant to last.

4.name: Saubhagya
4.title: Good fortune
4.meaning: A favourable yoga, traditionally good for celebrations and family matters.

5.name: Shobhana
5.title: Splendour
5.meaning: A favourable yoga, traditionally good for beauty, travel and joyful events.

6.name: Atiganda
6.title: Great difficulty
6.meaning: Traditionally an unfavourable yoga; important beginnings are usually avoided.

7.name: Sukarma
7.title: Good deeds
7.meaning: A favourable yoga, traditionally good for honest work and helping others.

8.name: Dhriti
8.title: Steadiness
8.meaning: A favourable yoga, traditionally good for patient, lasting work.

9.name: Shula
9.title: The spear
9.meaning: Traditionally an unfavourable yoga, linked with friction; best kept for routine tasks.

10.name: Ganda
10.title: The knot
10.meaning: Traditionally an unfavourable yoga; tradition advises caution and avoiding new ventures.

11.name: Vriddhi
11.title: Growth
11.meaning: A favourable yoga, traditionally good for anything you want to grow: savings, learning, gardens.

12.name: Dhruva
12.title: The constant
12.meaning: A fixed, favourable yoga, traditionally good for lasting foundations.

13.name: Vyaghata
13.title: The blow
13.meaning: Traditionally an unfavourable yoga, linked with conflict; a day to act gently.

14.name: Harshana
14.title: Delight
14.meaning: A favourable yoga, traditionally good for celebration and good news.

15.name: Vajra
15.title: The thunderbolt
15.meaning: A forceful yoga that tradition treats with caution, especially for travel.

16.name: Siddhi
16.title: Accomplishment
16.meaning: A favourable yoga, traditionally good for completing and succeeding.

17.name: Vyatipata
17.title: Calamity
17.meaning: One of the most avoided yogas in tradition; important beginnings are postponed.

18.name: Variyana
18.title: Comfort
18.meaning: A favourable yoga, traditionally good for ease, comfort and generosity.

19.name: Parigha
19.title: The iron bar
19.meaning: Traditionally an obstructive yoga; best for steady work rather than new starts.

20.name: Shiva
20.title: Benevolent
20.meaning: A favourable yoga named after Shiva, traditionally good for prayer, study and learning.

21.name: Siddha
21.title: Ready
21.meaning: A favourable yoga, traditionally good for beginning things with confidence.

22.name: Sadhya
22.title: Achievable
22.meaning: A favourable yoga, traditionally good for practice and steady progress.

23.name: Shubha
23.title: Auspicious
23.meaning: A favourable yoga, traditionally good for ceremonies and good beginnings.

24.name: Shukla
24.title: Brightness
24.meaning: A favourable yoga, traditionally linked with clarity and honest dealings.

25.name: Brahma
25.title: Expansive wisdom
25.meaning: A favourable yoga, traditionally good for learning, teaching and study.

26.name: Indra
26.title: Leadership
26.meaning: A favourable yoga, traditionally good for authority, public matters and recognition.

27.name: Vaidhriti
27.title: Division
27.meaning: Like Vyatipata, one of the most avoided yogas in tradition; a day for routine.

1.name: Bava
1.title: Strength for beginnings
1.meaning: A moving karana, traditionally good for starting things and for steady work.

2.name: Balava
2.title: Learning and ritual
2.meaning: A moving karana, traditionally good for study, prayer and religious work.

3.name: Kaulava
3.title: Friendship
3.meaning: A moving karana, traditionally good for friends, family and partnerships.

4.name: Taitila
4.title: Home and comfort
4.meaning: A moving karana, traditionally good for the home and family matters.

5.name: Garaja
5.title: Fields and building
5.meaning: A moving karana, traditionally good for practical work, land and building.

6.name: Vanija
6.title: Trade
6.meaning: A moving karana, traditionally good for buying, selling and business.

7.name: Vishti
7.title: Bhadra — a pause
7.meaning: The one moving karana tradition avoids: important beginnings wait until it ends.

8.name: Shakuni
8.title: The bird
8.meaning: One of four fixed karanas that come only around the new moon. Tradition keeps important beginnings for later.

9.name: Chatushpada
9.title: The four-footed
9.meaning: A fixed karana at the new moon, traditionally linked with animals and with offerings to ancestors.

10.name: Naga
10.title: The serpent
10.meaning: A fixed karana at the new moon, traditionally kept for hard, lasting tasks rather than new starts.

11.name: Kimstughna
11.title: The first sliver
11.meaning: The first karana after the new moon and the last of the four fixed ones. Tradition gives it a quiet, steady character.

0.name: Ravivara
0.title: Sunday — the Sun's day
0.meaning: Ruled by the Sun. Traditionally a day for confidence, leadership and honouring light.

1.name: Somavara
1.title: Monday — the Moon's day
1.meaning: Ruled by the Moon. Traditionally a gentle day for home, care and feelings.

2.name: Mangalavara
2.title: Tuesday — Mars's day
2.meaning: Ruled by Mars. Traditionally a day of energy and courage, and of care around conflict.

3.name: Budhavara
3.title: Wednesday — Mercury's day
3.meaning: Ruled by Mercury. Traditionally a day for learning, writing, trade and communication.

4.name: Guruvara
4.title: Thursday — Jupiter's day
4.meaning: Ruled by Jupiter, teacher of the gods. Traditionally a day for wisdom, teachers and generosity.

5.name: Shukravara
5.title: Friday — Venus's day
5.meaning: Ruled by Venus. Traditionally a day for beauty, art, relationships and pleasure.

6.name: Shanivara
6.title: Saturday — Saturn's day
6.meaning: Ruled by Saturn. Traditionally a day for discipline, patience and finishing work.

restFullMoon.name: Purnima rest
restFullMoon.title: A full-moon rest day
restFullMoon.meaning: Tradition kept three days of rest around each full moon: the day before, the day itself and the day after. Many use them as slower days and for celebration.

restNewMoon.name: Amavasya rest
restNewMoon.title: A new-moon rest day
restNewMoon.meaning: Tradition kept two days of rest around each new moon. A natural time to slow down and turn inward.

ekadashi.name: Ekadashi
ekadashi.title: Ekadashi — a lighter day
ekadashi.meaning: The 11th day of each half of the lunar month, sacred to Vishnu. Traditionally kept by fasting or eating lightly; many simply keep it as a quieter, simpler day.

uttarayana.name: Uttarayana
uttarayana.title: The Sun's northward half-year
uttarayana.meaning: From the December solstice the Sun moves north. Tradition sees this half-year as a time of growth, learning and outward effort.

dakshinayana.name: Dakshinayana
dakshinayana.title: The Sun's southward half-year
dakshinayana.meaning: From the June solstice the Sun moves south. Tradition sees this half-year as a time of reflection and turning inward.

ritu1.name: Vasanta
ritu1.title: Spring
ritu1.meaning: The season of renewal, roughly mid-February to mid-April. Tradition calls it the king of seasons, a time of festivals and fresh starts.

ritu2.name: Grishma
ritu2.title: Summer
ritu2.meaning: Long, hot days, roughly mid-April to mid-June. Tradition favours slower afternoons and simple routines.

ritu3.name: Varsha
ritu3.title: The rains
ritu3.meaning: The monsoon season in India, roughly mid-June to mid-August. Tradition sees a time for staying close to home, study and retreat.

ritu4.name: Sharad
ritu4.title: Autumn
ritu4.meaning: Clear skies and bright moons, roughly mid-August to mid-October. Tradition celebrates harvests and the great Navaratri festivals.

ritu5.name: Hemanta
ritu5.title: Early winter
ritu5.meaning: Cool and settled, roughly mid-October to mid-December. Tradition sees a season of stability, gathering and warmth at home.

ritu6.name: Shishira
ritu6.title: Late winter
ritu6.meaning: The coldest season, roughly mid-December to mid-February. Tradition sees a time of rest and of waiting for spring.

sheets.tithi: A tithi is a lunar day: the time the Moon takes to pull a little further ahead of the Sun (12°, one thirtieth of a full circle). Because the Moon's pace varies, a lunar day lasts about 19 to 26 hours and can begin at any hour. A lunar month has 30: fifteen while the Moon grows (Shukla) and fifteen while it shrinks (Krishna).
sheets.nakshatra: The band of sky the Moon travels along is divided into 27 equal sections, each named after a star or star group in it. The Moon passes through about one section a day. Each section has a guardian deity and its own meaning, shown on the day screen.
sheets.yoga: Add up how far the Sun and the Moon have each travelled around the sky, and the total falls into one of 27 equal sections: that section is the yoga. It changes about once a day. Each yoga has its own name and meaning, shown on the day screen. Tradition avoids four of them (Atiganda, Ganda, Vyatipata, Vaidhriti) for important beginnings.
sheets.karana: A karana is half a lunar day, so each lunar day has two. There are eleven kinds: seven repeat in turn through the month, and four come only around the new moon.
sheets.vara: The weekday. In the traditional calendar it runs from sunrise to sunrise, not from midnight. Each day belongs to one of the seven heavenly lights seen by eye: Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus or Saturn, the same ones behind the names Sunday, Monday and Saturday. That light decides which name the day's Choghadiya (hour by hour) starts with.
sheets.brahma: Brahma Muhurta, "the creator's hour", is the 48 minutes that begin about an hour and a half before sunrise. Tradition holds it the best time for meditation and prayer.
sheets.abhijit: Abhijit Muhurta, "the victorious hour", is about 48 minutes around local midday, when the Sun is highest. Tradition holds it good for an important beginning, such as a journey or new work, except on Wednesdays, so VedaCal does not show it then.
sheets.rahuKaal: Split the time from sunrise to sunset into eight equal parts, each about an hour and a half; Rahu Kaal is one of them, a different one each weekday. Rahu is the shadow that, in myth, swallows the Sun during an eclipse. Tradition does not start journeys, businesses, big purchases or ceremonies in this time; work already under way can continue.
sheets.yamaganda: Yamaganda is one of the eight equal parts of the daylight, each about an hour and a half, a different part each weekday. It is named after Yama, the god of death and judgement. Tradition avoids starting new ventures, journeys or big money decisions in it; routine work and prayer can go on.
sheets.gulika: Gulika (Gulikai) is one of the eight equal parts of the daylight, each about an hour and a half, a different part each weekday, and is linked to Saturn. Drik Panchang and Shubh Panchang list it with Rahu Kaal and Yamaganda as an unfavourable time: no contracts are signed, no big purchases made and no money invested in it.
sheets.choghadiya: Choghadiya splits the day (sunrise to sunset) and the night (sunset to the next sunrise) into eight parts each, about an hour and a half long, and gives each part one of seven names. Three are good (Amrit, Shubh, Labh), one is neutral (Chal) and three are best avoided (Udveg, Rog, Kaal); their order depends on the weekday. It is popular in North and West India for choosing a time to travel or start something, and a good part that falls in Rahu Kaal is still avoided.
sheets.rhythm: The traditional rhythm follows the Moon and the Sun: rest days around the full and new moon, the Ekadashi fast twice a month, six seasons instead of four, and two half-years, as the Sun's path moves north after the December solstice and south after the June one.
sheets.times: All times are for {city} and calculated on your device. Sunrise is when the top edge of the Sun appears, the same rule as Drik Panchang, the most widely used online Hindu calendar. VedaCal's times differ from it by less than 2 minutes.
sheets.about: VedaCal shows the traditional Hindu lunar calendar (Panchang) in plain words. Everything is calculated on your device and nothing is sent anywhere. The guidance describes tradition and is not medical or professional advice. City data © GeoNames, CC BY 4.0.
sheets.masa: A lunar month lasts one cycle of the Moon, about 29.5 days, so it begins on a different Western date each year. A month takes its name from the sign the Sun moves into during it (when the Sun enters Aries, it is Chaitra). The names themselves were given long ago after the star near which the month's full moon falls (Chaitra from Chitra, Kartika from Krittika); today the match is only approximate. VedaCal counts months from full moon to full moon, as in North India; South and West India count from new moon to new moon, so for half of each month the name there is one behind. About every three years an extra month (Adhika) is added so that the calendar keeps pace with the seasons.
sheets.rashi: The Sun and the Moon move through the twelve signs of the zodiac. Vedic astrology ties the signs to the stars, Western astrology to the seasons, and over the centuries the two have drifted about 24°, almost a whole sign, apart. So a Moon in Gemini by the Vedic count is often in Cancer by the Western one. Choose which one VedaCal shows in Settings.
sheets.parana: Ekadashi is a fast kept twice a month and ended the next day. VedaCal shows when to end it: not too early, because the first quarter of the twelfth lunar day (Hari Vasara) still counts as part of the fast, and not too late, while the twelfth lunar day (Dwadashi) is still running. Usually that is the first few hours after sunrise (the first fifth of the daylight). When Hari Vasara runs long, the time moves to the afternoon (the fourth fifth), because tradition avoids midday. VedaCal shows the exact time on the day screen.
sheets.eclipse: By tradition, no new work is started and no meals are eaten during an eclipse (Grahan), and the time is given to prayer or meditation. VedaCal shows the moment of greatest eclipse and whether any of it can be seen from your location.
sheets.sankranti: Sankranti is the moment the Sun moves into the next sign of the Vedic zodiac, twelve times a year. Each one opens a solar month; Makara Sankranti in mid-January, a harvest festival, is celebrated across India.
sheets.pushya: Pushya, "nourishment", is one of the Moon's 27 star sections and is held the most favourable of them. When the Moon is in Pushya on a Thursday (Guru Pushya) or a Sunday (Ravi Pushya), tradition sees that time as good for beginnings, for buying gold and for starting to learn. The times shown are when the two overlap.
sheets.amritSiddhi: Amrit Siddhi, "nectar of success", forms when a weekday meets its own Moon star: Sunday with Hasta, Monday with Mrigashira, Tuesday with Ashwini, Wednesday with Anuradha, Thursday with Pushya, Friday with Revati, Saturday with Rohini. It comes one to three times a month, and tradition holds it among the most favourable times to begin something. The times shown are when the two overlap.
sheets.sarvarthaSiddhi: Sarvartha Siddhi, "success in every aim", forms when the weekday and the Moon's star are one of about thirty traditionally helpful pairs. It is common, about ten days a month, so VedaCal shows it on the day screen only and does not mark it on the month. The times shown are when the two overlap.

ui.skyLegendOrbit: Inner ring: the 30 lunar days (Tithi) of 12°, counted from the Sun. The lighter half is waxing, the darker half waning. “New moon” and “full moon” mark where the Moon stands at those moments.
ui.skyLegendStars: Middle ring: the 27 Moon stars (Nakshatra). The one the Moon is in now is highlighted.
ui.skyLegendSigns: Outer ring: the 12 signs (Rashi). Blue is the Moon’s sign, gold the Sun’s.
ui.skyLegendNote: Seen from above, not to scale: only the directions are true. From above, the Moon’s lit half always faces the Sun; from Earth we see part of it, a crescent or a full disc. The Moon and the Sun move counter-clockwise.
ui.creditDrik: times, festivals and fast days are checked against it
ui.creditMypanchang: second check of lunar day, star and yoga end times
ui.creditShubh: Rahu Kaal, Yamaganda, Gulika and Choghadiya explained
ui.creditArxiv: origin of the lunar month names
ui.notice.polar: The Sun does not rise or set here today, so the Panchang day cannot be divided. Moon information is still shown.
ui.locationError: Your location is not available. Search for a city instead.
ui.zodiacNote: Vedic signs follow the stars; Western signs follow the seasons and sit about one sign ahead.
ui.legendRestNote: Around the new and the full moon
ui.legendEkadashiNote: The 11th lunar day, twice a month
ui.legendEclipseNote: By tradition, nothing new is started
ui.installNote: Adds VedaCal to your home screen. It then opens like an app and works without internet.
ui.guideInstallIntro: VedaCal works in the browser, but once installed it opens from its own icon like any app and works without internet.
ui.guideInstallAndroid: Android (Chrome): open Settings in VedaCal and tap “Install app”. No button there? Open Chrome’s menu (three dots, top right) and choose “Add to Home screen”.
ui.guideInstallChrome: If Chrome says VedaCal is already installed when it is not, use the button in Settings: Chrome can mistake it for another app from the same website.
ui.guideInstallIphone: iPhone and iPad (Safari): tap Share (the square with an arrow — at the bottom on iPhone, at the top on iPad), scroll down and choose “Add to Home Screen”.
ui.guideUseDay: Day — the Moon today, the day’s good times and times to avoid, and its facts. The ‹ › arrows change the day; “Today” brings you back.
ui.guideUseTap: Tap any name — the Moon, a time, a fact — to read what it means.
ui.guideUseMonth: Month — the Moon’s shape on every day, rest days, fast days and special days. Tap a day to open it.
ui.guideUseSky: Sky — where the Sun, the Moon and the star sectors stand, seen from above. Press play to watch them move.
ui.guideUseSettings: Settings — your city or your location, language, Vedic or Western signs, 12- or 24-hour clock, and theme.
ui.guideOfflineText: After the first visit VedaCal keeps its own copy on the phone, about 2 MB: it opens instantly, calculates without internet and sends nothing anywhere. When a new version is out, it downloads in the background and a bar offers to update. To remove the app, press and hold its icon and choose Uninstall. Your city and settings live only on this phone, so removing the app removes them too.
ui.guideGlossaryIntro: Every name the app uses, in plain words. Open one to read what it means and, where it has them, all its values.
ui.cancelOut: Abhijit and {name} cancel each other out

amrit.name: Amrit
amrit.title: Nectar
amrit.meaning: Ruled by the Moon, the best of the seven. Tradition holds it good for any kind of work, prayer, travel or celebration.

shubh.name: Shubh
shubh.title: Auspicious
shubh.meaning: Ruled by Jupiter. Traditionally good for ceremonies, above all weddings, and for prayer and business.

labh.name: Labh
labh.title: Gain
labh.meaning: Ruled by Mercury. Traditionally good for starting study, learning a skill, trade and money matters.

chal.name: Chal
chal.title: Moving
chal.meaning: Ruled by Venus and neutral. Its restless nature makes it traditionally suited to travel, not to ceremonies.

udveg.name: Udveg
udveg.title: Unease
udveg.meaning: Ruled by the Sun. Traditionally avoided for new work and journeys, though held suited to dealings with government.

rog.name: Rog
rog.title: Friction
rog.meaning: Ruled by Mars. Traditionally avoided for anything new; held suited only to contests and facing opponents.

kaal.name: Kaal
kaal.title: Loss
kaal.meaning: Ruled by Saturn. Traditionally no auspicious work begins in it, though it is held suited to work that builds savings.
